.²1 <ab>N.</ab> of one of the wild aboriginal tribes in India, such as hunters,
 fishermen <ab>&c.</ab>; a mountaineer; {#mA nizAda pratizWAM tvamagamaH SASvatIH#}
 {#samA#} <ls>Rām. 1. 2. 15</ls>; <ls>R. 14. 52</ls>, <ls n="R. 14.">70</ls>; <ls>U. 2. 5</ls>.
.²2 A man of a degraded tribe in general, an outcast, a Chāṇḍāla.
.²3 Especially, the son of a Brāhmaṇa by a Śūdra woman; <ab>cf.</ab> {#brAhmaRAdvESyakanyAyAmambazWo#}
 {#nAma jAyate . nizAdaH SUdrakanyAyAM yaH pAraSava ucyate ..#} <ls>Ms. 10. 8</ls>.
.²4 (In music) The first (more properly the last or seventh) note of the
 Hindu gamut; {#gItakalAvinyAsamiva nizAdAnugatam#} <ls>K. 31</ls> (where it has sense 1 also).
.²5 <ab>N.</ab> of a Kalpa.

The rule according to which when a compound expression
 is capable of being dissolved as a {#karmaDAraya#} or a {#tatpuruza#},
 the former is to be preferred to the latter. This is discussed and established
 by {#jEmini#} and {#Sabara#} in <ls>MS. 6. 1. 51-52</ls> in connection with the
 expression {#nizAdasTapati#}.
